strategy.summary: Reproduce SciPy’s correctness bug in `scipy.signal.minimum_phase(..., method="homomorphic")` where Nyquist-frequency parity handling is reversed for odd/even `n_fft` (notably N=963 vs 964). The test should fail on the buggy commit d2a1c1ce1f2e and pass on the fixed revision by asserting that the magnitude spectrum of the minimum-phase signal matches the original magnitude spectrum at all rFFT bins (within dtype-specific `atol`).

pip_packages: numpy (version not constrained in evidence; install a NumPy version compatible with SciPy build)
system_packages: BLAS/LAPACK dev libs if required by the SciPy build system
build_commands: python -m pip install pybind11==2.13.6 cython==3.0.12 pythran==0.17.0 pytest
# Install/ensure SciPy-openblas (OpenBLAS 0.3.28) as documented for this issue/PR; the build must link against it:
export OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=Haswell  # if your OpenBLAS package supports this; otherwise omit
export NPY_BLAS_ORDER=???  # only if your build system requires it
python -m pip install -e . --no-build-isolation  # build SciPy from source on both buggy and fixed revisions
pinned_because: scipy-openblas/OpenBLAS 0.3.28 (DYNAMIC_ARCH NO_AFFINITY Haswell MAX_THREADS=64) is numerically relevant in the evidence and must be the same toolchain family to match the observed failure mode (dependency constraint explicitly provided).
pybind11==2.13.6 is explicitly required by the evidence for the reproducer build dependencies.
cython==3.0.12 is explicitly required by the evidence for the reproducer build dependencies.

strategy.reproducing_test: Run the `test_nyquist` test shown in the provided diff (or ensure your local checkout includes the same test change). It should exercise `minimum_phase(h, method="homomorphic", n_fft=N, half=False)` for N in (963, 964) and dtype in (float32, float64), then compare magnitude spectra of the original FIR and its minimum-phase version via rFFT.
strategy.success_criterion: The test `test_nyquist` must FAIL on SciPy built from the buggy revision `d2a1c1ce1f2e` and PASS on the fixed revision from PR #24749 (the same test should pass after applying the PR’s fix). The transition is: `xp_assert_close(error, xp.zeros_like(error), atol=atol)` fails on buggy and succeeds on fixed for the same environment/toolchain.
strategy.numerical_probe: The test computes `H_mag = abs(rfft(h, N))` and `H_min_mag = abs(rfft(h_min_sig, N))`, with `error = H_mag - H_min_mag`. It asserts `error` is (elementwise) close to zero within `atol` (float32: 1e-5, float64: 1e-13). The bug manifests as nonzero `error` (a Nyquist-parity-related ripple) causing the assertion to fail.

input_output_examples.input: N=963; dtype=float32 or float64; fc=10; fs=100; h=firwin(N, fc, window="hann", pass_zero="lowpass", scale=False, fs=fs); h_min_sig=minimum_phase(h, method="homomorphic", n_fft=N, half=False); compare abs(rfft(h,N)) vs abs(rfft(h_min_sig,N)).
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Test assertion fails because `error = H_mag - H_min_mag` is not within `atol` (no exact numeric outputs provided in the evidence).
input_output_examples.expected_output: After fix, `error` is within `atol` for all rFFT bins; thus the `xp_assert_close` succeeds for N=963 and N=964 (no exact numeric outputs provided in the evidence).

risks: This defect is explicitly tied to the OpenBLAS configuration family in the evidence; if you build/link SciPy against a different BLAS/LAPACK (or a different OpenBLAS version/config), the failure may not reproduce or may fail differently.
The evidence does not specify NumPy pinning; an incompatible NumPy could change the floating-point behavior enough to alter pass/fail thresholds, especially for float32.

The evidence mentions tolerances were chosen empirically; if the fixed behavior still exceeds the chosen atol in your CI environment, you may need to mirror the PR’s exact atol logic (already included in the diff) and ensure the same build/CPU settings.
The test relies on `scipy.fft.rfft` via `from scipy.fft import rfft`; ensure SciPy build includes the FFT backend expected by this repo.
If the fix PR includes additional changes beyond Nyquist bin parity (not shown in the context), ensure you check out the correct fixed revision rather than attempting an ad-hoc local patch.

oracle.reference_source: The project’s own regression test `test_nyquist` (as provided in the diff) comparing rFFT magnitude spectra of the FIR and its homomorphic minimum-phase transform.
oracle.why: Success/failure is determined solely by whether the elementwise magnitude difference `error` is within the hardcoded tolerance; no separate numeric value is required.

fails_on_buggy.description: What the assertion sees on the buggy revision, and why that makes it fail
fails_on_buggy.value: On d2a1c1ce1f2e, `test_nyquist` produces `error` that is not elementwise close to zero for at least one of the parameter combinations (notably for odd N=963 and/or even N=964 depending on parity handling). This makes `xp_assert_close(error, zeros_like(error), atol=atol)` fail because the Nyquist/bin weighting bug yields a non-negligible spectral ripple in the magnitude comparison.

passes_on_fixed.description: What the assertion sees on the fixed revision
passes_on_fixed.value: On the fixed revision from PR #24749, the Nyquist-frequency parity logic in the homomorphic minimum-phase mask is corrected, so `error` becomes elementwise sufficiently small to satisfy `atol` for both N=963 and N=964 across float32/float64, making the same assertion succeed.
